newsitem.title: ALBANIA: OSCE warns Albania against marring poll process.
newsitem.headline: OSCE warns Albania against marring poll process.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe warned Albanian President Sali Berisha and all political parties on Thursday against putting obstacles in the way of the electoral process.

Expressing deep concern over developments in Albania, the OSCE chairman, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen, said the future of international assistance to Albania depended on Albanian authorities cooperating in the process of democratic reform.

"The chairman-in-office of the OSCE wishes...to express his deep concern with the latest developments in Albania," Petersen said in a statement. "The chairman...would like to urge President Berisha and all parties involved to cease forthwith any attempt to put obstacles in the way of the electoral process."
The OSCE supervised the monitoring of Sunday's first round of elections and declared that, despite some problems, voting was "adequate and acceptable."

The OSCE also plans to spearhead international economic and financial assistance to the Balkan state once a new government is formed. The Socialists appear on track to win the election, ousting Berisha's Democrats from power.

But Petersen warned: "The chairman...of the OSCE wishes to underline that the future of international assistance to Albania will depend on the willingness of the Albanian authorities to cooperate on democratic reform."
